To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the staphylococcus phage repressor (CI), its N-terminal domain (rNTD), and C-terminal domain (rCTD) are well-ordered proteins, and their urea-induced denaturation proceeds via two intermediates.
the dimerization ability and the stability of rCI, rCTD, and rNTD are different from each other and that the urea-induced equilibrium denaturation of these proteins occurs in a multiphasic manner.
the CI and the domains are folded by the same multiphasic pathway and that the stability of the dimeric form of rNTD is slightly higher than that in rCI and rCTD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and stability of a stably folded phage CI and its domains.
the dimerization ability, the denaturation mechanism and the stability of the staphylococal phage repressor CI and its NTD and CTD.
the folding and the stability of rCI and its domains, and it provides a new insight into the mechanism of the CI-mediated lysogenization of phage φ11 in S. aureus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stability order of CI, N-terminal, and C-terminal domain is rCI > rNTD >  rCTD.
CI is an intrinsically disordered protein and that its folding proceeds via a multiphasic pathway.
the CI and NTD are folded by a multiphasic pathway, and the stability and dimerization of CI and its domains differ significantly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CI is more stable in the dimer form than in the monomeric form, and its NTD, which is less stable than CI and rCTD in the dimer state, is responsible for the CI dimerization.
the CI dimer is more stable than the monomers of its domains, but rCTD or rNTD is slightly more stable than rCI.
the CI and NTD, like CTD, are folded by the multiphasic mechanism and their dimers are more stable than monomers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CI and NTD are more stable than the CTD.
rNTD and rCTD are stable and well-folded proteins and can form dimers.
the dimerization ability of CI, rNTD and rCTD is not a prerequisite for the formation of their intermediates.
